overall.headline: Storm and very big surf arrive tonight at home; a global Microsoft outage and Iran–US strikes are the world's main stories.
overall.bluf: Pacifica: no outages, closures or official emergency orders. A High Surf Warning starts at 6 PM today and runs to 4 AM Sunday, with a Coastal Flood Advisory Saturday and rain with gusts to 39 mph today; stay well away from the shoreline. Abroad, Microsoft's Outlook/Teams outage is unresolved after about 12 hours, and Iran says it hit a US radar in Bahrain after a US strike. Nothing here calls for stocking up.

local.note: Rain and wind today; dangerous surf from 6 PM.

regional.note: Sierra storm warnings; storms continue next week.

world.note: US–Iran strikes in Gulf; Microsoft outage; Ukraine talks.

changes: Beach Hazards Statement now in force today (to 6 PM); High Surf Warning follows from 6 PM to Sunday 4 AM, with waves above 35 ft possible per KQED.
Forecast rain today ½–¾ in with gusts to 39 mph and a chance of thunderstorms; a second storm arrives Sunday and a third mid-week.
New: Microsoft outage (Outlook, Teams, Copilot) since Thursday ~8 AM Pacific, still unresolved; Microsoft says it is not a cyberattack.
New: Iran says it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain (unverified) after a US strike in Sirik; tanker reportedly hit a mine in Hormuz.
Dropped as stale: Spain strike, Taiwan sorties, Ecuador, Kenya Ebola, Japan quake cluster (no new reports).

coming_up.title: Rain, gusts to 39 mph, possible thunderstorms
coming_up.detail: About ½–¾ in of rain; SF peak tide near noon–1 PM adds coastal flood risk.

coming_up.title: High Surf Warning on the coast
Second storm: rain Sunday, ¼–½ in
coming_up.detail: Rain mainly after 10 AM Sunday; South wind to 24 mph.

coming_up.title: I-580 Richmond–San Rafael Bridge closure
coming_up.detail: Caltrans closure for toll-booth removal work; expect detours if you cross the North Bay.

coming_up.title: Hwy 1 full maintenance closure in San Francisco
Third storm: rain likely Tue night through Wed

home_front.summary: High Surf Warning from 6 PM today to Sun 4 AM; Coastal Flood Advisory Sat; no IPAWS alerts.

items.title: High Surf Warning: stay off Pacifica beaches, piers and rocks
items.detail: NWS has a Beach Hazards Statement until 6 PM today, then a High Surf Warning from 6 PM to 4 AM Sunday and a Coastal Flood Advisory Saturday. KQED reports waves possibly above 35 ft, strong rip currents and sneaker waves; a storm surge of about a foot adds erosion risk. NWS's marine model shows ~5–6 ft max waves with 15-second periods, so long-period sets can run far up the beach.
items.action: Don't go to the beach, pier, jetty or bluff edge to watch waves; keep children and dogs away. Avoid Beach Blvd and Rockaway/Linda Mar parking lots near the shoreline if surf is washing over.
items.when: Now to Sat; warning Fri 6 PM – Sun 4 AM
items.where: Pacifica coast, Linda Mar, Sharp Park

items.title: No significant earthquakes near home
items.detail: Nothing of magnitude 3 or more within 350 km this week; the largest nearby was M2.6 near Aromas. The tsunami center's latest bulletin (Nov 11) was for a quake off Vancouver Island with no tsunami threat to California.

home_front.summary: No PG&E or water notices found; wind and rain today could cause scattered outages.

items.title: Rain, gusty wind and possible thunderstorms today
items.detail: Rain likely from about 7 AM, with showers and thunderstorms 10 AM–1 PM. South-southwest wind 20–26 mph, gusts to 39 mph; ½–¾ in of rain. Wind of this strength sometimes causes scattered power outages; I found no reported outages yet.
items.action: If power goes out, report it at pge.com/outages and keep phones charged. Don't drive through standing water.

home_front.summary: Hwy 1 open; flaggers near Montara today; wet roads and surf spray possible.

items.title: Hwy 1 one-way traffic control near Montara today
items.detail: Caltrans drainage work (one lane, flaggers) south of the tunnels is scheduled for today. Allow extra time in rain. A full Hwy 1 maintenance closure in San Francisco is set for Mon–Tue (Nov 16–17).

home_front.summary: Air quality good (AQI ~39); no local health advisories.

items.title: Air quality good
items.detail: US AQI is about 39 now, peaking near 61 (moderate) Saturday evening. Fine for everyone.

items.title: FDA recalls: sausage-egg-cheese biscuit sandwiches; cheddar
items.detail: Fresh To You sausage, egg & cheese biscuit sandwiches (Nov 8) and Family Farmstead Dairy cheddar (Nov 10, Listeria) are recalled. Check the FDA page for where each was sold.

home_front.summary: No local shortages. WTI ~$89, Brent ~$96; Hormuz still disrupted.

items.title: Oil steady; Hormuz traffic still restricted
items.detail: WTI is about $88.6 and Brent $96.1, both roughly flat on the day. Iran says 12 tankers have been hit in 12 days and insurers are pulling cover; airlines expect higher fares from jet-fuel costs.

default.task: Charge phones and battery packs and set out flashlights today.
default.why: Gusts to 39 mph and storms through mid-week raise the chance of a night-time outage.

3d.task: Fill a few water jugs and check three days of shelf-stable food and medication.
3d.why: Back-to-back storms could briefly cut roads or power.

3w.task: Check you have three weeks of prescriptions and pet food on hand.
3w.why: A cheap buffer before wet weather makes errands harder.

3m.task: Rotate the oldest stored food and water into this week's use.
3m.why: Large stores only help if they're still good when you need them.

1y.task: Test your backup power or radio and check fuel or battery levels.
1y.why: With food covered, power and communications fail first.

ladder.summary: Quiet apart from the storm and surf; see Home front.

items.title: Surge and big waves raise bluff erosion risk
items.detail: With about a foot of storm surge on top of big surf, KQED warns of added erosion on the coast. Bluff-edge buildings and trails are most exposed.
items.action: Stay back from bluff edges and closed trails; report new cracks or slumping to the city.

ladder.summary: Sierra storm warnings and a super El Niño winter ahead.

items.title: Winter Storm Warnings in the Sierra
items.detail: NWS has warnings from 10 AM today: Tahoe/Mono to Saturday 10 AM; Yosemite, Kings Canyon and Sequoia to Tuesday 4 AM. Expect heavy snow and chain controls on mountain passes.
items.action: If driving to Tahoe or Yosemite this weekend, check Caltrans QuickMap and carry chains or delay.

items.title: 'Super El Niño' means a stormier winter
items.detail: KQED reports record ocean heat off San Francisco and says a strong El Niño is under way; forecasters say the Bay Area could see 2–10 in over the second half of November.

items.title: California voters pass Prop. 5 on recall elections
items.detail: CalMatters reports voters overhauled recall rules; Democrats gained seats in the Assembly. No effect on households.

ladder.summary: Global Microsoft outage; Congress summons Nvidia's ex-CEO; Iran-linked threats.

items.title: Microsoft outage disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide
items.detail: The outage began about 8 AM Pacific Thursday and was still unresolved this morning; Microsoft calls fixes 'marginal success' and says it is not a cyberattack. Reports cite disruption in 74 countries including some government offices.
items.action: If you rely on Outlook or Teams for bills, appointments or work, use phone or another service and check your bank or medical portals directly.

items.title: Actively exploited bugs in Outlook, Chrome and others
items.detail: CISA added 11 flaws to its must-patch list Nov 6–10, including Microsoft Outlook, Google Chromium, Cisco and Barracuda products.
items.action: Update Chrome/Edge and install Windows and Office updates this week.

items.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO summoned by Congress over alleged Chinese spy tie
items.detail: Jensen Huang resigned Thursday; the Senate Banking Committee has summoned him and Commerce Secretary Lutnick to testify. Nvidia's CFO is interim CEO.

items.title: FBI: North Korean hackers stole $400m with fake video calls
items.detail: More than 900 victims were targeted by the 'FaceStealer' scheme. Treat unexpected video-call software installs as suspect.

items.title: Brooklyn building collapse kills eight
items.detail: Two children and two construction workers are among the dead in Flatbush. No Bay Area impact.

items.title: Markets calm; 10-year yield at 5.1%
items.detail: S&P 500 is down 0.35%, VIX is 18.3 (below 25), oil is flat, gold is up 0.4% but down 4.3% over five days. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.10%, up 2.1% on the day.

ladder.summary: Ukraine strikes deep as US brings Europe into talks; storm in Iberia.

items.title: Ukraine fires nearly 1,200 drones at Russia; Russian warship hit in Baltic
items.detail: Reports describe one of Ukraine's largest drone raids as US-led talks widen to European security. A Ukrainian drone also hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, reportedly a first in open Baltic waters. Zelensky welcomes Europe joining the talks.
items.action: Nothing to do; if Baltic escalation or NATO involvement is confirmed, watch fuel and gas prices.

items.title: Bomb-hoax threats force more Italian school evacuations
items.detail: Authorities say the threats are hoaxes; no real risk has been found.

items.title: Storm Charles floods southern Europe
items.detail: Floods and flight cancellations in Portugal and southern Spain; travelers should check airline status.

ladder.summary: Pakistan border militancy and Indonesian political strain.

items.title: Pakistan says it killed 74 'terrorists' in raids
items.detail: Tensions with Afghanistan are rising after more border attacks. The count is the military's claim.

items.title: Indonesia's vice president resigns
items.detail: The resignation came as his eligibility and academic credentials were questioned, and signals strain in President Prabowo's alliance.

items.title: M5.8 quake off Papua New Guinea
items.detail: USGS says it struck last night off Kavieng; GDACS rates it green with few people affected, and no tsunami.

ladder.summary: US–Iran exchange of strikes with no deal; Gaza hospitals and shelters strained.

items.title: Iran says it hit a US radar in Bahrain after a US strike
items.detail: Iran's Guards claim they destroyed a US early-warning radar and say a tanker hit a mine in Hormuz; neither is independently verified. Trump says 'we don't need a deal' but called more strikes 'quite unlikely'; Iran awaits a reply to its seven-point proposal via Qatar.
items.action: If large-scale US strikes resume, expect higher fuel prices; fill the car's tank.

items.title: IAEA cannot verify Iran's underground enrichment plant
items.detail: A confidential IAEA report says Iran won't resume inspections while under military threat.

items.title: Gaza: rain threatens power and health care; aid groups seek shelters
items.detail: After an Israeli strike on a hospital killed six on Thursday, aid groups say each rainfall risks cutting power to what remains of health services.
